note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

unit.title: Plan to undertake a routine task

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: A work order says: 'Add two 110 V outlets in the staff room, Block C.' What should you find out before you list the materials?
options: Which circuit will feed them, and its spare capacity
Which colour of cover plate the staff like best
How many outlets the staff room had last year
Whether the outlets can be fitted without boxes

questions.stem: While planning, you find that the new outlets would go on a circuit that already feeds a refrigerator and a microwave. What is the best action?
options: Fit them anyway, as the drawing was approved
Check the load and raise it with the supervisor
Move the refrigerator to another room yourself
Fit a bigger breaker so the circuit will not trip

questions.stem: A job card only says 'Fix lights in the canteen'. Why is this not enough to plan from?
options: It does not give the date that the canteen was built
It does not list the tools you already own
It does not say which lights or what the fault is
It does not say how many people eat there

questions.stem: The specification asks for all new wiring in conduit, but the drawing shows sheathed cable clipped to the wall. What should your plan do?
options: Use clipped cable, because it is quicker to fit
Use whichever method the stores have more of
Mix both methods so both documents are met
Note the conflict and get a written ruling first

questions.stem: Which document tells you the rating, mounting height and fixing method for a new outdoor flood light?
options: The maker's installation instructions
The building's fire evacuation plan
The supplier's delivery note
The Centre's attendance register

questions.stem: Before you plan a new circuit in an existing building, why do you read the board schedule (the chart that lists each circuit)?
options: To find which way of wiring is the cheapest
To see what each breaker feeds and what is spare
To find out who last painted the board cover
To check the dates on the building's insurance policy

questions.stem: The as-built drawing of a building is very different from what you see on site. Which should your plan follow?
options: The drawing, because the engineer has approved it
Whichever one makes the job quicker to finish
What is on site, after reporting the difference
An older drawing that is kept in the office

questions.stem: Put these steps for replacing a faulty outdoor light in order: 1 test and switch on, 2 isolate and prove dead, 3 remove the old fitting, 4 fit and connect the new fitting.
Why should a plan for rewiring a classroom block do the rooms in a sequence that keeps some lights working each day?
options: So the school can still use part of the block
So the new cables do not need testing after
So fewer breakers are needed in the board
So the work can be done without isolating

questions.stem: Why should you visit an office before planning a new 220 V air-conditioning circuit for it?
options: To choose the temperature the staff will set
To find the cable route, board space and fixings
To pick the colour of the indoor unit for them
To find out how much the owner is willing to spend

questions.stem: A step in your plan reads 'Make good the wall after chasing'. What does 'make good' mean?
options: Test the cable that is buried in the wall
Make the wall stronger than it was before
Repair the surface so it is neat again
Paint the whole room in a new colour

questions.stem: You will work on one circuit in a busy office. Why must the plan say which breaker is locked off, and by whom?
options: So the office manager can switch it back on again
So the breaker can be changed while it is off
So no voltage tester is needed on the day
So the right circuit is made dead and stays dead

questions.stem: When does your plan say the voltage tester must be checked on a proving unit?
options: Before and after proving the circuit dead
Only once, when the tester is first bought
Only after all of the work is finished
Only if the tester's battery seems weak

questions.stem: A routine task needs a whole building switched off at the main switch. What should the plan include?
options: A note to switch off fast before anyone notices
An agreed shutdown time, told to all affected
Leaving the main on and working each circuit live
Asking the guard to switch off when he has time

questions.stem: Three electricians will work on the same isolated board. How should the plan say it is locked off?
options: One lock, with its key left in the board door
No lock, as a warning sign is enough
Each person fits their own lock to it
One lock, with the key hidden nearby

questions.stem: For changing lamps in a warehouse ceiling 6 m high, which access equipment should the plan choose?
options: A step-ladder standing on two pallets
A long ladder leant on the shelf racks
A strong table with a chair on top
A tower scaffold or lift, used by trained staff

questions.stem: The job is in a ceiling space under a zinc roof at midday. Which control should the plan include?
options: Short work spells, drinking water and airflow
Working faster to finish before lunch
Wearing a heavy jacket against the heat
Taking off PPE so the body stays cool

questions.stem: You will drill into a concrete ceiling to fix a new light. What should the plan check first?
options: That the drill bit is the cheapest in stock
That no cables or pipes are buried there
That the ceiling was painted this year
That the light is the same make as before

questions.stem: Which PPE should the plan list for cutting chases in a block wall with a wall chaser?
options: An arc-flash suit and a hard hat only
Rubber boots only, because of the dust
Eye, ear and dust protection, and gloves
A welding helmet and a full leather apron

questions.stem: A cable run is 18 m from the board to the farthest outlet, with 3 m extra for drops and terminations. You add 10% for waste. How much cable should you plan?
Each new outlet needs two fixing screws. You plan 14 outlets, and screws come in packs of 20. How many packs must you order?
Why should a materials list give the cable size and type, not just 'cable'?
options: So the stores can charge a higher price
So the right cable for the load and site comes
So the cable can be any colour in stock
So less cable needs to be ordered

questions.stem: The plan needs 20 mm conduit, but it is on back order for two weeks. What is the best action?
options: Use garden hose in its place for now
Use 16 mm conduit and force the cables in
Tell the supervisor and agree a change
Start without conduit and add it later

questions.stem: Why should the plan check the voltage and frequency marked on new equipment before it is bought for a Jamaican building?
options: Jamaican supplies are all 240 V only
Equipment never states its own voltage
Every building here is three-phase
So it matches the 110 V or 220 V, 50 Hz supply

questions.stem: Which instrument should be booked in the plan to check a new circuit's insulation before it is switched on?
options: An insulation resistance tester
A clamp meter
A sound level meter
A light meter

questions.stem: A job has four steps of 1.5 h, 2 h, 45 min and 30 min, plus 15 min to test. How long is that in total?
options: 4 h 30 min
5 h
5 h 15 min
4 h 45 min

questions.stem: A school says the power can only be off from 3 p.m. to 6 p.m. Your work needs 4 hours dead. What should the plan do?
options: Work live after 6 p.m. so that the job finishes
Start at 3 p.m. and hope to finish in time
Split it into dead stages that fit the time
Switch off at noon without telling anyone

questions.stem: Why does an experienced electrician add some spare time (contingency) to a routine plan?
options: So the client pays for hours not worked
So trainees can take a longer lunch
So no time estimate is needed at all
Small problems often turn up on site

questions.stem: Boxes must be fixed before cables are pulled, and cables pulled before they are terminated. What does this tell you about the plan?
options: These steps must follow one another
These steps can all be done at once
Terminating can start on the first day
The boxes can be fixed at the very end

questions.stem: Painters will work in the rooms where you are fitting outlets. What is the best plan?
options: Fit the plates first and let painters work round
Agree an order so plates go on after painting
Ask the painters to paint over the outlets
Leave the boxes open until someone complains

questions.stem: You lead two trainees on a routine job. Which is the best way to share out the tasks?
options: Let them choose whatever they like doing
Give all the hardest tasks to the newest trainee
By what each can do safely, with your checks
Do all the work yourself so it is quicker

questions.stem: Before the work starts, what should you tell the people who use the building?
options: How the circuits are wired inside the board
The cost of each item on the materials list
The full names of everyone in your training group
When power will be off and which areas lose it

questions.stem: A client wants the work done on Saturday, when the office is empty. What must the plan make sure of?
options: Access, keys and help nearby are arranged
The work can be done without isolating
No tester is needed at the weekend
The job card can be skipped this time

questions.stem: Which tests should the plan list for a new outlet circuit before it is switched on for use?
options: A look to see that each plate is straight
Continuity, insulation resistance and polarity
A check that the breaker handle is the right colour
Plugging in a kettle to see if it boils

questions.stem: Why should a plan include a hold point before a ceiling is closed over new cables?
options: So the ceiling boards can dry out first
So the client has time to choose the light fittings
So hidden work is inspected while it can be seen
So the cables can cool down after pulling

questions.stem: Which record should be filled in when a new circuit is tested?
options: The trainee attendance register for that whole day
The store's stock list for cable and boxes
The building's visitor log at the gate
A test sheet with the readings and tester's name

questions.stem: Halfway through the job, you find that an existing circuit has no earth conductor. What should you do?
options: Stop that part, make it safe and report it
Carry on, as earthing is not in your job
Join the earth to the neutral at the outlet
Connect the earth to a nearby water pipe

questions.stem: The client wants a cheaper light fitting than the one in the specification. What is the right step?
options: Fit it, since the client is the one paying
Get the change agreed and recorded first
Refuse and leave the site straight away
Fit the specified one and charge more

questions.stem: The planned cable route is now blocked by a new steel beam. What should you do?
options: Drill through the beam to keep the planned route
Run the cable loose across the floor
Find another safe route and get it agreed
Tape the cable to the side of the beam

questions.stem: How can a team leader best check progress against the plan during a two-day job?
options: Wait until the very end and then see what got done
Ask the client if it seems to be going well
Count the empty cable reels each hour
Compare work done with the schedule at set times

questions.stem: Before a circuit is handed back to the client, who should remove the lock and tag?
options: The person who fitted them, after checks
Anyone in the team who has finished
The client, when they come in
The security guard at closing time

questions.stem: Your job adds a new circuit to a board. What should happen to the board schedule?
options: Leave it, as the old one is close enough
Update it to show the new circuit
Throw it away and start a new board
Write the new circuit on the wall

questions.stem: Your completion report only says 'job done'. What else should a Level 3 hand-over report include?
options: Your own views about the client
How the trainees spent their lunch
Test results, defects found and advice
A list of tools you would like to buy

questions.stem: A job took 2 hours longer than planned. Why should the reason be written down?
options: So someone can be blamed for the delay
So the client can be charged extra
So the plan never needs to be checked again later
So the next plan for this kind of job is better

questions.stem: Three jobs come in: a sparking outlet in a classroom, a new outlet for a printer, and a scratched board cover. Which should be planned first?
options: The sparking outlet
The printer outlet
The board cover
Whichever is quickest

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the name of the chart, often fixed inside the board door, that lists each circuit and what it feeds?
A circuit needs 25 m of cable and you allow 20% extra. How many metres of cable do you plan for?
What is the name of the signed form that controls who may work on a main switchboard, and when?
What is the name of the small device fitted over a breaker handle so that a padlock can hold it in the off position?
A 110 V circuit will feed loads of 600 W, 450 W and 600 W at the same time. What total current, in amps, will it carry?
What is the name of the device used to check that a voltage tester is working, before and after proving dead?
An electrician takes about 15 minutes to fit each light fitting. How many hours will 24 fittings take?
What do we call the drawing that shows a building's wiring as it was actually installed?
In what unit is the rating of a circuit breaker given?
When checking the load, you find a 220 V heater that draws 11 A. What is its power in watts?
What name is given to the visit made before planning, to look at the cable routes, the board and the site conditions?
Which type of breaker switches both line conductors of a 220 V circuit at the same time?
A plan says 'install 9 outlets'. Each outlet needs 3.5 m of cable on average. How many metres of cable is that in total?
What is the name of the stage of wiring when boxes and cables are put in, before the walls are finished and accessories fitted?
What is the name of the stage when switches, outlets and fittings are connected after the walls are finished?

essays.stem: You are asked to add a 220 V air-conditioning circuit to an office at the Centre. Describe how you would plan the job, from receiving the work order to the day the work starts.
essays.modelAnswer: First I read the work order and the maker's instructions for the unit, to find its voltage, current and the breaker size it needs. I visit the office to find the board, check that it has space for a two-pole breaker and enough spare capacity, and choose a safe cable route. I work out the cable size for the load and the length of the run, then list the materials with quantities and a little extra. I write a short method statement and a risk assessment covering safe isolation, work at height, drilling and dust. I estimate the time for each step and agree a date and a shutdown time with the office, because their power will be off. I book the tools and test instruments, including a voltage tester and proving unit. Finally I go over the plan with my supervisor and get it approved.
markingPoints: Reads the work order and the maker's data (voltage, current, breaker size)
Surveys the site: board space, spare capacity, cable route
Works out cable size and length and lists materials
Method statement and risk assessment, including safe isolation
Agrees timing and shutdown with the client and gets the plan approved

essays.stem: Explain how you would plan the safe isolation for a routine task on a board that also feeds other people's work areas, and how you would make sure the circuit stays dead while you work.
essays.modelAnswer: I would use the board schedule and testing to find exactly which breaker feeds the circuit, because the chart may be wrong. I would tell the people in the other areas what will be switched off and when. On the day I switch off the breaker, fit my own lock to it with a lock-off device, and fix a tag with my name, the date and the reason. If more than one person works on the circuit, each fits their own lock on a hasp. I check my voltage tester on a proving unit, test between all conductors and earth at the point of work to prove it dead, then check the tester again on the proving unit. The key stays with me. Only I remove my lock, after the work is finished and checked and everyone is clear.
markingPoints: Identifies the right circuit, not trusting the chart alone
Informs the people affected
Switch off, lock off with own lock, and tag
Proves dead with a tester checked on a proving unit before and after
Keeps the key; only the person who locked off removes the lock

essays.stem: Explain how you would work out the materials for a small installation from a drawing. Use the example of six outlets on one new circuit.
essays.modelAnswer: I start from the drawing and the specification, which give the outlet positions, the cable type and the wiring method. I count the items: six outlet boxes, six outlets and six cover plates, plus one breaker in the board. I measure the cable route on the drawing using its scale, from the board along the route to each outlet, and add the drops down the walls and some length for each termination. For example, if the run measures 30 m with drops, I add about 10% for waste, so I order 33 m. I then add the fixings, clips or conduit and fittings, grommets, and any labels. I check what is already in stock and write a materials list with the size, type and quantity of each item, so the right things are ordered and delivered.
markingPoints: Uses the drawing and specification for positions, cable type and method
Counts the items (boxes, accessories, plates, breaker)
Measures the route to scale and adds drops and terminations
Adds an allowance for waste, with a worked figure
Writes a list with size, type and quantity, checked against stock

essays.stem: Describe how you would plan a routine electrical job that must be done while a school or business keeps working, so that disruption is kept low and everyone stays safe.
essays.modelAnswer: I would meet the person in charge to learn their working hours and the times when power can be off. I would split the work into stages, so that only one area or circuit is dead at a time and the rest of the building keeps working. Any shutdown would be agreed in writing and told to staff in good time, with a notice. Noisy or dusty work such as drilling would be planned for times when rooms are empty. I would plan barriers and signs round the work area, keep tools and cables out of walkways, and make sure ladders are never left standing alone. Each day I would leave the area safe and tidy, with no exposed live parts, and tell the person in charge what is finished and what comes next.
markingPoints: Finds out working hours and when power may be off
Splits work into stages so only one area is dead at a time
Agrees and announces shutdowns in advance
Barriers, signs and clear walkways; noisy work at quiet times
Leaves the area safe each day and updates the person in charge

essays.stem: Explain how you would brief and supervise two trainees on a routine job of replacing lamps and fittings in a corridor, and how you would check their work.
essays.modelAnswer: Before we start, I go over the plan with them: the steps, who does what, the circuit to be isolated, the ladder or tower to be used and the hazards. I ask them questions to check that they understand. I give each one tasks that they can do safely, and I do the isolation with them so they see it done properly, with locks, tags and a tester checked before and after. During the work I stay close, especially for work at height and for connections, and I correct anything unsafe straight away. When each fitting is done, I check the connections are tight, the earth is connected and the fitting is secure before it is closed up. At the end we test the circuit together and I record the results and give them feedback.
markingPoints: Briefs the steps, roles and hazards, and checks understanding
Shares tasks by what each can do safely
Shows and supervises safe isolation
Stays close for risky steps and corrects unsafe acts
Checks each fitting, tests, records and gives feedback

essays.stem: Explain the inspections and tests you would plan before handing over a new outlet circuit, and say why each one is done.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would plan a visual inspection with the circuit isolated, to check that the cable is the right size, is supported and protected, that boxes are fixed and that the connections are tight with no bare copper showing. Then I would plan the dead tests. A continuity test of the earth conductor proves that every outlet is joined to earth, so a fault will trip the breaker. An insulation resistance test checks that there is no breakdown between conductors or to earth, which could cause shock or fire. A polarity check proves that line, neutral and earth go to the right terminals and that the breaker is in the line. Only after these pass would the circuit be switched on and checked with a socket tester. All results go on a test sheet.
markingPoints: Visual inspection while isolated, with reasons
Earth continuity, and why
Insulation resistance, and why
Polarity, and why
Live checks only after dead tests pass; results recorded

essays.stem: Halfway through a planned job you find something unexpected, such as an old circuit with no earth or a cable damaged by rats. Explain what you would do and how you would change the plan.
essays.modelAnswer: I would stop work on that part, because carrying on could leave a dangerous installation. If anything could be live or unsafe, I would make it safe by isolating it, locking it off and tagging it. I would record what I found, with photos, and report it to my supervisor and then to the client, explaining the danger in plain words. Together we would decide what extra work is needed, such as replacing the damaged cable or running a new earth. I would work out the extra materials, time and cost and get the change agreed in writing before doing it. Then I would update the plan and the schedule, tell the team about the change, and include the fault and what was done in the completion report.
markingPoints: Stops work on the affected part
Makes it safe: isolate, lock off, tag
Records and reports to supervisor and client
Works out extra materials, time and cost and gets written agreement
Updates the plan, briefs the team and records it in the report

essays.stem: Compare a job card, a method statement and a risk assessment. Say what each one contains and why a routine electrical task needs all three.
essays.modelAnswer: A job card says what the task is, where it is, who asked for it and by when, and is signed off when the work is done. A method statement sets out the steps of the work in order, the tools and materials, and how safe isolation and testing will be done. A risk assessment lists the hazards of each step, such as electric shock, falls from ladders, dust and burns, who could be harmed, and the controls that will be used. A routine task needs all three because the job card tells you what to do, the method statement tells you how to do it, and the risk assessment makes sure it is done safely. Routine jobs are where people take short cuts, so written plans keep everyone to the safe way.
markingPoints: Job card: what, where, who, by when, sign-off
Method statement: ordered steps, tools, isolation and testing
Risk assessment: hazards, who is at risk, controls
Why all three are needed together
Routine work invites short cuts; written plans prevent them

essays.stem: Explain how you would estimate the time for a routine electrical task and build a simple schedule with spare time. Use an example.
essays.modelAnswer: I break the job into steps and estimate each one from past jobs or the time sheets. For example, to add three outlets: isolate and prove dead 15 minutes, fix boxes 45 minutes, run and clip cable 60 minutes, terminate 30 minutes, inspect and test 30 minutes, clean up 15 minutes. That is 3 hours 15 minutes. I add about 15% for problems such as hard drilling, which gives about 3 hours 45 minutes. I put the steps in order on a simple schedule or bar chart, showing which ones must wait for others, such as testing after terminating. I check the schedule against the times when the power can be off and when the client is free. During the job I compare progress with the schedule and tell my supervisor early if it is slipping.
markingPoints: Breaks the job into steps and estimates each from experience or records
Correct worked total for the example
Adds a sensible contingency
Orders the steps, showing which depend on others
Fits to the client's times and monitors progress

essays.stem: Describe what a completion report and hand-over should contain for a routine electrical task, and explain how reviewing the finished job improves future planning.
essays.modelAnswer: The completion report should say what work was done, where, on which circuits and on what dates. It should include the test results, any defects found that were not fixed, and any advice to the client, such as a circuit that is near its limit. It should list the materials used and the hours worked, and note any changes agreed during the job. At hand-over I show the client what was done, explain any new switches or breakers, give them the updated board schedule and test sheet, and get the job card signed. Afterwards the team reviews the job: what went well, what took longer than planned and why, and what was missing from the materials list. These notes make the next plan for a similar job more accurate and safer.
markingPoints: Report states work done, circuits and dates
Includes test results, defects and advice
Includes materials, hours and agreed changes
Hand-over: explains to client, gives updated schedule and sheet, sign-off
Review of what went well or badly feeds the next plan

practical1.title: Survey a site and plan a routine circuit addition for approval
practical1.brief: The assessor gives the group a work order to add a new circuit (for example two 110 V outlets and one light) to a room at the Centre. As a group, survey the room and its board, then produce a full plan: a sketch of the cable route with measurements, a materials list with sizes and quantities, a costed list using the J$ prices the assessor gives, a method statement, a risk assessment, a safe isolation plan, and a timed schedule with spare time. Share the work so each member writes at least one document, and each member checks one document written by someone else. The group then presents the plan to the assessor, who acts as the supervisor and asks questions. No covers are removed and nothing is switched off during the survey. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical.
materials: Copy of the room layout or a blank sheet for sketching
Board schedule for the room's board
Blank method statement, risk assessment and schedule forms
Price list in J$ from the assessor
photos: The group at the room, measuring the cable route
The board schedule and board, viewed with the cover on
The finished route sketch with measurements
The method statement and risk assessment
The schedule and the isolation plan
The group presenting the plan to the assessor
checklist: Took part in the survey and recorded accurate measurements
Wrote at least one planning document clearly and correctly
Worked out quantities and costs correctly, with an allowance for waste
Included safe isolation (switch off, lock off, tag, prove dead with a tester checked before and after) in the plan
Identified the main hazards and suitable controls
Checked another member's document and corrected errors
Answered the assessor's questions about the plan
safety: Do not open any board or remove any cover during the survey
Keep walkways clear and do not stand on furniture to measure
Use a step-ladder only if the assessor allows it, with someone footing it
Follow the Centre's rules for working in occupied rooms

practical2.title: Plan, lead, install, test and report a routine task on a training bay
practical2.brief: The assessor gives the group a job card to install a small circuit on a training bay (for example one light controlled by one switch, and one outlet, fed from a training board). Plan the job first: steps, roles, materials, time and hazards. Then carry it out. Each member leads one stage (isolation and proving dead, fixing and cable running, terminating, inspection and testing, or report and hand-over) while the others work under that person's direction. All work is done with the bay's supply isolated, locked off and tagged, and proved dead with a tester checked on a proving unit before and after. The group carries out dead tests (continuity and insulation resistance) and records them; the assessor does any live check. Finish with a completion report and hand the job over to the assessor. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical.
materials: Training bay with its own isolator and training board
Cable, boxes, switch, outlet and lamp holder as the job card lists
Job card, plan, test sheet and completion report forms
photos: The group's written plan and roles
The bay locked off and tagged, with the tester on the proving unit
Terminations inside the switch and outlet boxes, before the plates go on
The completed test sheet and completion report
checklist: Followed the plan and the agreed roles
Isolated, locked off, tagged and proved dead with a tester checked before and after
Led their stage clearly and safely
Fixed and connected work neatly, with correct terminations and earth connected
Carried out and recorded the dead tests correctly
Noted any problems or changes and how they were handled
Helped complete the report and left the bay clean and tidy
safety: Never work on a live bay; only the person who fitted a lock removes it
Check the tester on the proving unit before and after proving dead
Wear safety glasses when drilling and cutting
Only the assessor energises the bay for a live check, with everyone clear
